channel.title: NVIDIA Corporation — recent CVEs
channel.description: Most recent CVEs assigned by NVIDIA Corporation (nvidia).

item.title: CVE-2026-100962 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️
item.description: NVIDIA NeMo Export-Deploy for all platforms contains a vulnerability in multimodal deployment where an attacker could cause a server-side request forgery. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might cause information disclosure.

item.title: CVE-2026-65168 · 7 HIGH
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains an attacker-controlled heap-based buffer overflow in the slurmstepd socket handling code.

item.title: CVE-2026-65165 · 5.3 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains a vulnerability where a user could deliberately alter the provided nodelist alongside the --distribution=arbitrary option to gain access to compute nodes outside of the current job allocation.

item.title: CVE-2026-65140 · 5.7 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains some inconsistent authorization checks against the Operator permission level in the SlurmDBD that can be chained together in a way that would permit an Operator to make themselves an Administrator.

item.title: CVE-2026-65139 · 6.3 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains an attacker-controlled SQL injection attack in certain SlurmDBD RPCs that can lead to arbitrary code execution.

item.title: CVE-2026-65138 · 6.3 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains an attacker-controlled arbitrary-memory read in the slurmstepd socket API that could be used to ex-filtrate authentication keys.

item.title: CVE-2026-65109 · 4.7 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm is subject to a symlink resolution issue in the container cleanup code that could allow an attacker to remove files outside of their control on the compute node.

item.title: CVE-2026-65108 · 6.3 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains an attacker-controlled heap-based buffer overflow in the slurmstepd process while the slurmstepd is running with root permissions.

item.title: CVE-2026-65107 · 6.3 MEDIUM
item.description: NVIDIA Slurm contains a vulnerability where a user could alter the supplemental group list as part of an sbcast file transmission to write a file to a path they would not normally have access to.
